audit.whatIsWrong: The page's central instruction is to time Blinding Assault on his auto wind-up 'so his autos miss', including inside Counter Strike. It also calls his ultimate 'R Counter Strike' twice, conflating E and R.
audit.why: Riot's Blinding Assault text says Valor marks an enemy and hinders its vision — it does not make attacks miss, so the whole 'blind his autos through E' plan is built on an effect Quinn does not have. Counter Strike already dodges attacks by itself for its duration and then stuns; its stun also ends Behind Enemy Lines, which is a flagged channel.
audit.corrected: Rewrote the plan around spacing and Counter Strike's 17s cooldown instead of a blind, separated E from the ultimate, and added the channel cancel.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing warned that Counter Strike's stun ends your ultimate.
audit.why: Behind Enemy Lines carries the interruptible-channel flag.

edits.before: Jax can't catch you at levels 1-2, so abuse it — your range and Harrier auto-resets let you auto, leap in with the Harrier proc, and walk out before his Q-W can land. The key tool all lane is Blinding Assault (Q): time it on his auto windup, because Jax leans on basic attacks even inside E, and the blind makes those autos whiff. Don't dump Q at max range where he just walks through it — hold it for when he commits a gap-close.
edits.after: Jax can't catch you at levels 1-2, so abuse it — your range and Harrier auto-resets let you auto, Vault in for the Harrier proc, and leave before Leap Strike lands. The tool that decides the lane is Counter Strike: for its duration your autos simply do not land, and it stuns after, so never spend a trade into it and count its 17 seconds at rank 1. Blinding Assault hinders his vision, so use it on the step-up, not at max range.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are still yours: keep shoving with Q, take plates, and trade with Vault (E) to slow him and refresh Harrier for a second leap. The danger flips at 6 — his R Counter Strike maxes out and he can E-dodge your autos then Q-W stun-burst you, so respect his all-in when your Q blind is on cooldown. Don't facecheck or get pinned against the wall; instead use your own R to roam, crash the wave, and convert your lane lead into kills bot or mid rather than greeding a 6-on-6 fight.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are still yours: keep shoving with Blinding Assault, take plates, and trade with Vault (12s) to slow him and reposition. The danger flips at 6 — his ultimate lands and he can dodge your autos through Counter Strike, then Leap Strike and stun-burst you, so respect the all-in whenever Vault is down. Don't facecheck or get pinned on a wall; use your own R to roam, crash the wave, and convert the lane lead into kills bot or mid.

notes: Name conflict to resolve: this brief's packet lists Jax's R as 'Grandmaster-at-Arms' while the audited mirror (jax__quinn) states it corrected five fields to 'Grandmaster's Might'. The two sides of the same matchup now disagree on the ultimate's name, so I referred to it as 'his ultimate' everywhere rather than pick a side — see questionsForUser. Also note the same Behind Enemy Lines data artefact the mirror flagged: cd 3 in the kit file is the Skystrike value, not the ultimate's cooldown, so no number was printed for it.
